name: Locations overlay — competitive monitoring
initialPrompt: Graphics overlay for a 25fps talking-head clip (host narrating an Apify -> Zapier -> Power BI competitive-monitoring use case). One opaque data panel anchored to the right ~40% of the frame (clear of the host's face and laptop) whose content MORPHS through the script beats: a 48-dot location grid where one dot flares orange on "bleeding"; flat report/dashboard rows that average the problem away; an Apify -> Zapier -> Power BI pipeline diagram with a flow pulse and a "~15 min" chip; a manual cursor ticking row-by-row that collapses to "1 zip / 1 day"; an auto-refresh loop; then the grid returns with a weekly sweep, surfaces a few flagged locations, and the panel recedes to a small apify.com corner bug. Designed to be exported with a transparent background (ProRes/qtrle strips the still backdrop) and composited over the real footage. No fade from/to black. Opaque cards, orange-only accent.
scriptWithTimestamps:
[00:00.16–00:03.20] One of your 48 locations has been bleeding orders for three weeks.
[00:03.76–00:08.40] Brand level reports won't catch it, and the delivery platform dashboards won't either.
[00:08.40–00:12.96] An Apify, Zapier and Power BI pipeline will in about 15 minutes.
[00:12.96–00:21.60] Most competitive monitoring still needs someone to manually pull listings location by location, and even then you're only seeing one zip code on one day.
[00:21.60–00:23.36] A system that runs itself doesn't.
[00:24.00–00:32.48] What we're building today refreshes every location's competitive position weekly, surfaces the ones that need attention, and stays out of your way the rest of the time.
